title: The Whiskey Rebellion
subtitle: Western Pennsylvania, 1791–1794
description: The 1791 federal tax on whiskey, the uprising against it in western Pennsylvania, and how it ended without a battle. Four pours.

pours.name: Old Overholt Straight Rye
pours.notes: A brand that began in Westmoreland County, one of the four counties at the centre of the rebellion, in the years after 1794.

pours.name: Pikesville Straight Rye
pours.notes: A Maryland rye name. Maryland was one of the four states that sent militia west in 1794. It is 110 proof, so try it with water.

pours.name: Michter’s US*1 Straight Rye
pours.notes: The name comes from an old distillery in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania. The company now distills in Louisville.

pours.name: Elijah Craig Small Batch
pours.notes: Named for a Baptist preacher in Kentucky. A later legend credits him with the first bourbon, on no good evidence.
